mcqs.q: On a tongue slide, the lingual papillae are essentially:
opts: Extensions of stratified squamous epithelium over lamina propria
mcqs.explain: Papillae are extensions of stratified squamous epithelium over lamina propria; deep in the section are interlacing skeletal muscle strands.

mcqs.q: Deep to the papillae in a tongue section you would identify:
mcqs.explain: The body of the tongue is skeletal muscle; interlacing muscle strands are seen deep in the section.

mcqs.q: Filiform papillae are recognized by being:
opts: Pointed and keratinized, with no taste buds
mcqs.explain: Filiform papillae are pointed, keratinized extensions of epithelium and contain no taste buds.

opts: Mushroom-shaped, non-keratinized, with taste buds on the surface
mcqs.explain: Fungiform papillae are mushroom-shaped, covered by thin non-keratinized epithelium, with taste buds on the superior surface.

mcqs.q: Immediately below a circumvallate papilla on a slide, you can identify:
opts: Serous glands (of von Ebner) opening into the surrounding furrow
mcqs.explain: Below a circumvallate papilla are the von Ebner serous glands, whose ducts open into the furrow that surrounds the papilla.

mcqs.q: Taste buds of the circumvallate papilla open into the:
opts: Lumen of the furrow surrounding the papilla
mcqs.explain: The pale taste buds line the lateral walls and open into the lumen of the furrow (sulcus) that surrounds the circumvallate papilla.

mcqs.q: On histology, taste buds appear as:
opts: Pale, barrel-shaped clusters within the epithelium
mcqs.explain: Taste buds are pale, barrel-shaped (ovoid) clusters of cells within the epithelium, contrasting with the surrounding cells.

mcqs.q: A taste bud opens to the surface through a:
mcqs.explain: A taste bud opens at a taste pore, through which dissolved substances reach the gustatory cells.

mcqs.q: The cells of a taste bud include taste-receptor (gustatory), supporting, and:
opts: Basal cells (which synapse with an afferent nerve)
mcqs.explain: A taste bud contains gustatory (receptor) cells, supporting cells and basal cells, synapsing with an afferent nerve fibre.

mcqs.q: Which papilla type is keratinized and therefore carries NO taste buds?
mcqs.explain: Filiform papillae are keratinized and lack taste buds; the other papillae are non-keratinized and bear taste buds.

mcqs.q: On a section, the circumvallate papilla is distinguished from a fungiform papilla by its:
opts: Large size and surrounding furrow with von Ebner glands
mcqs.explain: The circumvallate papilla is large and sits in a furrow (sulcus) with von Ebner glands below, unlike the small mushroom-shaped fungiform papilla.

mcqs.q: Taste buds are most numerous on the lateral walls of which papilla?
opts: The keratinized tip of filiform papillae
mcqs.explain: Many taste buds line the lateral walls of the circumvallate papilla and its vallum.

mcqs.q: The carpet of pointed papillae that gives the dorsal tongue its rough texture is formed by:
mcqs.explain: The numerous keratinized filiform papillae carpet the dorsum, giving it a rough, abrasive texture.

mcqs.q: The afferent nerve at the base of the taste bud functions to:
mcqs.explain: The afferent (gustatory) nerve fibre synapses with the receptor cells and carries taste impulses toward the brain.

saqs.q: How are lingual papillae oriented relative to the rest of the tongue section?
saqs.a: They are extensions of stratified squamous epithelium over lamina propria, above the deep interlacing skeletal muscle.

saqs.q: How do you identify filiform vs fungiform papillae?
saqs.a: Filiform: pointed, keratinized, no taste buds. Fungiform: mushroom-shaped, non-keratinized, taste buds on top.

saqs.q: What lies immediately below a circumvallate papilla, and where do its ducts open?
saqs.a: Von Ebner serous glands; their ducts open into the furrow (sulcus) surrounding the papilla.

saqs.q: Describe the histologic appearance of taste buds.
saqs.a: Pale, barrel-shaped clusters of cells within the epithelium, opening at a taste pore.

saqs.q: List the cells of a taste bud.
saqs.a: Gustatory (taste-receptor) cells, supporting cells, and basal cells, synapsing with an afferent nerve.

saqs.q: Which papillae carry taste buds and which do not?
saqs.a: Fungiform, circumvallate and foliate carry taste buds; filiform do NOT.
